Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

symptom.disease_info: Adjustment Disorder involves the development of emotional or behavioral symptoms in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor, emerging within about three months of the event and causing marked distress or functional impairment that is out of proportion to what would typically be expected. The disturbance is time-limited, usually resolving within six months after the stressor or its consequences end, and does not meet full criteria for another mental disorder such as major depressive disorder or PTSD. Clinically, patients often present with a clear narrative linking their difficulties to recent changes or stressors in relationships, work, health, or life transitions, and with noticeable decline in social, occupational, or academic functioning. It is differentiated from normal stress reactions by the degree of impairment and from other disorders by its temporal relationship to a stressor and subthreshold symptom patterns.

patient.stressor: After completing her associate’s degree in arts administration, Toni had been working part-time coordinating community workshops and events, with a plan to transition into a full-time role at a local arts nonprofit. Two months ago, the organization abruptly lost a key grant and froze all hiring, eliminating the position she had been informally promised and leaving her with only sporadic gig work just as her student loan payments were coming due and her lease was up for renewal. The sudden derailment of her carefully laid plans made it increasingly hard for her to follow through on commitments she normally thrived on—she started backing out of organizing the Harvard summer fair, stopped attending the improv meet-ups where she had once been a regular, and let emails about a potential Chicago residency go unanswered. When she missed a major deadline for a gallery collaboration she had proposed herself and found she could no longer bring herself to open her project planning software, her mother and a close friend from the Farmhouse Museum both expressed concern and helped her schedule an appointment at a local clinic, where she described feeling unable to handle how thrown off course she felt by the job situation.
patient.chief_complaint: After losing the job opportunity I was counting on, I feel like I’ve been reacting badly to everything and can’t cope with what’s happening in my life.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: Ever since the job at the nonprofit fell through, it’s like I’ve spiraled—small things like an email from my landlord or a text about a possible gig make my chest tighten, I shut my laptop, cancel plans, and just lie there crying or scrolling on my phone instead of dealing with anything.

add_requirements.within_3_months_of_stressor: All of this really started in the weeks right after they told me the full-time position was off the table and the grant was gone—I was doing okay before that, and then within a month or so I just couldn’t handle even simple things.
add_requirements.within_6_months_after_stressor_or_conseq: I keep telling myself that once I either sort out a stable job or decide on a different plan, this reaction can’t go on forever; it feels tied to everything being up in the air right now rather than some long-standing issue.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I’ve been so overwhelmed and avoidant, I’ve lost out on paid gigs, stopped showing up to my regular improv group, and even let my lease and loan emails pile up to the point where I’m worried I might miss payments or not have a place lined up to live.
add_requirements.duration: It’s been about two months now, ever since they told me the nonprofit job wasn’t happening, that I’ve been feeling this unable to cope and derailed.
